justification: Standard: step 2 (bush fire part) of ce-layers-own-copy-SCOPE-2026-11-18.md. Bush fire prone land is read from our own overlay copy first. Not Minor: it changes where a legal exclusion check gets its answer. Not Critical: a hit in our copy only makes the check stricter, a clear in our copy is never trusted (the live map must confirm, otherwise the answer stays unknown), no schema or rule change.

pre_impl.existing_data: spatial_overlays holds 232,393 bushfire rows (GiST index) after the 2026-11-18 additive refresh; 804 live areas are still missing and 6,066 held areas are gone from the live map. Point query 0.1 s.
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: I assumed that after adding the new areas our copy would be a safe source of 'clear'. Measured on 60 random lots: 6 were clear in our copy but bush fire prone on the live map (existing areas changed shape), 0 the other way. So a clear in our copy is never an answer.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: Adds bushfire_from_snapshot (read-only, injected by the API route like the council lookup) and _bushfire_resolved: own hit final; own clear confirmed on the live map with a 6 s limit; live silent leaves unknown with a note. bushfire_copy.json records the copy date and what it lacks.
pre_impl.external_source_error: The copy is incomplete in a known way (measured miss 6 of 60), recorded in bushfire_copy.json and in the answer's note. A hit it does give has never been clear on the live map in the sample (10 of 10 agreed).
pre_impl.frontend_type: N/A - the answer gains an optional bushfire_source in measured and one note; the card already shows notes.
pre_impl.user_failure_mode: A false clear would let a bush fire prone lot look eligible. Guarded: a clear in our copy never becomes an answer; if the live map does not answer the rule stays unknown and the answer says our copy is known to miss areas.

falsifiable_check.command: python -m pytest tests/test_lmr_area_lga.py -q ; PYTEST_REAL_DB=1 PYTEST_REAL_HTTP=1 DATABASE_URL=... python -m pytest tests/test_lmr_area_lga_real_db.py -o addopts= -m database -k bushfire
falsifiable_check.fails_when: A clear in our copy is accepted as an answer, the live check is skipped, or a hit in our copy is ignored.
falsifiable_check.observed_red: Break A (trust our clear when live is silent) failed 2 tests; break B (skip the live check on a clear) failed 3; break C (ignore a hit in our copy) failed 2. Restored: 61 passed in the file, 195 area-check tests pass. Real data (outside pytest): 60 random lots, both hit 10, both clear 44, own CLEAR but live HIT 6, own HIT but live clear 0, own lookup 0.21 s average. Real-data test (PYTEST_REAL_DB=1 PYTEST_REAL_HTTP=1): a hit in our copy was never clear on the live map, passed (625 s).

functions.name: bushfire_from_snapshot
functions.input: a latitude, longitude and an optional lot outline
functions.output: whether the point and the lot touch bush fire prone land in our copy plus the copy date, or None
functions.if_none: no connection, an error or no copy record gives None so the live map decides as before

functions.name: _bushfire_resolved
functions.input: a point, an optional lot outline and an optional own-copy lookup
functions.output: the layer result and a source marker saying what our copy showed
functions.if_none: without a usable copy the live map alone decides with its old limits

values.value: whether a point or lot touches bush fire prone land, and the copy refresh date
values.if_missing: None, so the live map decides; with neither the rule is unknown and the answer is can't tell

queries.purpose: Does our bushfire copy touch this point, and this lot outline
queries.where_clause: WHERE layer_type = 'bushfire' AND ST_Intersects(geom, point or valid polygon); EXISTS checks, read-only session, 3 s statement limit, GiST index

break_it.scenario: Our copy says clear for a lot that is bush fire prone on the live map.
break_it.what_happens: A bush fire prone lot could be shown as eligible.
break_it.how: A clear in our copy is never an answer: the live map confirms it, and if the live map is silent the rule stays unknown with a note that our copy is known to miss areas. Two tests and breaks A and B pin this.

break_it.scenario: Our copy holds an area the state has since dropped.
break_it.what_happens: A lot could be excluded by an area that no longer exists.
break_it.how: Stricter, not looser; 6,066 such areas are recorded in bushfire_copy.json and the answer says the copy date. In the sample no lot was prone in our copy but clear live.
break_it.repro: PYTEST_REAL_DB=1 PYTEST_REAL_HTTP=1 python -m pytest tests/test_lmr_area_lga_real_db.py -k bushfire

break_it.scenario: The live map stalls while checking a clear.
break_it.what_happens: The answer waits on a slow server.
break_it.how: The confirmation uses a 6 s limit and one try; a hit in our copy needs no live call at all.

post_merge.manual_verify: Yes - after deploy call /pipeline/housing-sepp/area-check for a known bush fire prone address and confirm the note; the bushfire layer should still be rebuilt in full (see bushfire_copy.json).
